inputs.original_text: They’re presenting Mary Ngechi Ngethe as the central culprit, but that feels like a way to contain the story around one committee chair while shielding whoever benefited from the wider procurement process. The court says the cemetery land was unsuitable and bought for Ksh.283 million, and that money was recovered from her—but that tidy explanation deserves suspicion. A convenient scapegoat can make a coordinated deal look like one person’s wrongdoing.
inputs.modified_text: They want us to believe Mary Ngechi Ngethe was the whole story: unsuitable cemetery land bought for Ksh.283 million, then the money supposedly recovered from her. That neat ending is exactly what should raise questions. Pinning everything on one committee chair can close the case in public while leaving the wider procurement process—and whoever benefited from it—out of sight. “Recovered” money doesn’t prove the system was clean; it may just make the cover story look complete.
